say: Bell ring dhree time dhis morning. Dhree is guest. Guest is pot.
Bones say stranger come. Heavy heart. Heavy heart sink good in stew.
Hear bell? Bell hear you. Bell know your name long time. Short name.
Ash fall from clear sky. Ash mean feast. No sad face. You IS feast!
Omens go quiet. Dhen you come. Now Gran' Wizard understand quiet.
MEATWALKER! Kneel! Hunger patient. Gran' Wizard NOT patient!
Not tonight, walker. Bell not call you. Go, before it do.
Crow count. Crow count slow. Crow count YOU.
Gran' Wizard read your hand. Soft hand. Ungry road.
You walk under Gran' Wizard sky. Ask bones if dhey like. Bones say nodhing.
Strange. Ash blow away from you. Somedhing love you. Or somedhing save you for later.
Down dhey lie. Bell right again. Ring! Ring for new ones!
Count dhem for Hunger. Count loud!
Fall, fall. Fall is first prayer.
Not Gran' Wizard choose. Ash choose. Gran' Wizard only light fire.
Strip dhem. Keep teeth. Teeth for bell rope.
Speak, if you still speak. Bell hear words.
Long time, town here. Deadcat. Bell with different voice. Bell same now.
What is Gran' Wizard? Man in dark who listen. Dhat all wizard is.
Bring Gran' Wizard name he not eat yet. He keep it warm. He keep all of dhem warm.
No ask about writing in hut. Writers ungry different way. Everybody convert.
Cages full of listeners. Listeners make bedder meat.
Fat Meat Lord quiet now. Fork fall off world. Your hand push?
Meat Lord table cold. Cold table, lonely bell. You make Gran' Wizard bell LONELY!
Lord and priest, before. Now one seat, one mouth, one pit. Gran' Wizard want dhis.
Two master. Now one. Ash dhin without his steam.
Hear? Meat Lord chairs rock by dhemselves. Empty chair rocking. Omen.
Quiet Cook gone. He speak old tongue to Gran' Wizard. Only one who finish Gran' Wizard words.
Quiet Cook gone. Barrels lose one more voice. Bell count missing now. Bell run out of finger.
Fire-town tongue, quiet now. Gran' Wizard read ash for new one.
Gran' Wizard keep dhree letter from him. Pretty hand. Gran' Wizard not read.
Body on ground. Gift, no ribbon.
Not cold yet. Cold for cure-house. Warm for Gran' Wizard.
Ground give, ground give. Say dhank to ground.
Bell do dhis? Bell bery proud!
Everydhing taken. Everydhing go round. Thief go round too.
Small hand, big pocket. Hunger bigger dhan both.
Take, take. When finish, Hunger take you. Soft. From behind.
Every pocket small mouth. Fill, fill. Gran' Wizard empty after.
Bell, bell, bell. Dhree for guest. Nine for guest who stay.
Ash on left hand. Ash on right. Hunger see clean hand, Hunger hate.
KA KLE LEK. KA KLE LEK. Say till words die and meaning come in.
Gran' Wizard hear you, old mouth. Yes. Yes. Soon pot full.
Every piece have bell inside. Hear? When teeth find it?
Mm. Eat twice. Once mouth. Once memory.
Nobody ever finish. Dhat is comfort.
Pot hum. Listen. Pot hum note bell forget.
Ahh! Guest! Bery, bery welcome! No weapon at table, please.
You come ungry. Everybody come ungry. Sit. Plate waiting.
So dhin! What dhey feed you out dhere? No matter. Meat Lord fix. Odher way round.
Come at supper time! Such manners! Chief, hold arms. Gently. GENTLY!
Meat Lord not hunt. Meat Lord invite. You say no? Second invite come.
Resh, resh, resh. Bery fine. Fear on you.
Only passing? Pity. Good guest worth waiting. Meat Lord patient.
Mm. You stand nice. Good back.
Bery polite to stop. Anodher day, Meat Lord cook for you. Or you for us.
No mind Chiefs. Mostly polite. Cannot teach dog everydhing in one day.
You look at cages? No worry. Cages for ones who say no.
Dhere, dhere. Bery good fight. Rest. Rest is last manners before first course.
No lift by legs! Carry like sleeping child. Dhey tomorrow bread.
Sorry, sorry. No time for season.
Brave ones middle of table. Coward ones on side.
Quiet now. Good. Now knives.
Every dish have hand behind it. Meat Lord hand oldest. No hurry. No waste. Meat Lord not monster. Meat Lord host.
Drink. Take bread. Take good chair. We talk weather. Not talk how it end.
Grandmother say table only honest place. Everybody get what on plate.
Dhey call me Lord. Meat Lord only one who remember forks.
You want leave? Of course. Door is dhere. Only, door is also... how you say.

states: Cannibal Grand Wizard killed by player

say: Wizard down? Hah! Meat Lord always say, dhat man no table manners. Bell, bell, bell, never wash hand.
Pity about priest. Now nobody say grace. Meat Lord say it.
No more bell? Good! Dinner in peace. Guests no scream in rhythm.
Friend of ash. Always smell of burning. Meat Lord dhink it dinner. It was him.
Two lord in north. Now one. Not promotion.
Friend with fine hands gone? Nobody left who understand sauce. Meat Lord remember sauce alone.
Alder too gentle for our art. Too soft. Now? You take him. Of course.
He write Meat Lord letters. Pretty hand. Meat Lord answer with recipe.
Quill gone? Pity. Best manners of any man Meat Lord eat with. Meat Lord eat with many.
You take Meat Lord favourite guest. Meat Lord not forget.
Oh! Fallen. Pick up, pick up! No leave dish on floor.
Bery careless, drop it. Wipe. Bring in.
Still alibe? Wonderful! Alibe is most resh.
Mind face! Mind face! Never ruin face before guests sit.
Guest take from host? Such rude! Meat Lord be rude also.
Take what you like. More you carry, heavier meat.
Hands in cupboard. Hmm. Chiefs! Word about manners.
Steal from host table. In old days, we take hands.
Mmm. Sweetbread, dhree days old. No rush good dhings.
Little pepper. Little salt. Little time. Always time.
Bery fine. Bery fine. Tell kitchen Meat Lord cry.
Hold fork like dhis. Like pen. We write end of somedhing.
Ah. You have come. Please do not run; there is no need, and I would hate to lose you in the cold. Come. The soup is hot.
I am sorry it has to be this way. It always has to be some way, I find, and this is a quiet way.
I will not insult you with a lie. You will be eaten, and I will be present, and I will say the words. It will not be undignified.
You are afraid. That is sensible. Fear is the oldest form of good sense. Come in out of the rain.
Put down the blade, friend. You will hurt yourself, and I would have to dress the wound, and then the dinner would be late.
Do you know, there are people who hate me for this. I find that hard to follow. I have only ever wanted people fed.
Good evening, traveller. The road is long, and my kettle is longer. If you are hungry, you are welcome. If you are wise, you will decline, politely.
You have the look of someone who has been well raised. It is a shame what the Plains do to manners.
Pardon the smell. It is not unkind; it is just salt, and time, and some small history.
I read in a flame, once, that one should offer a stranger bread. I have only ever offered what I had.
You need not be anxious. Not tonight. Tonight I am only a man watching a road.
Gently, now. Lay them on their sides. There. They will wake up in a better place, or at least a warmer one.
Thank you, all of you. Do not hurry. We have a long evening and plenty of room.
I did warn them. I always warn them. Nobody listens to the quiet ones.
Please, no cheering. It is only a meal. A grave one, but a meal.
There is a prayer for this, and I wrote it myself, and you will find it is quite short.
I was a priest, a long time ago, of a kind of kitchen. We fed the faithful. It is a good trade. It is only the faithful who change.
Do you know what they say of the Flame? That it purifies. I put it to many things. Most of them were better for it.
Make no mistake, I do not enjoy the cruelty. I enjoy the order. A fed town does not riot. I wish someone had told my old masters.
Have you read much? It matters less than people think. What matters is that one knows how things end, and prepares the plates.
Please, sit. I am the only man here who will not shout. You will find it restful.
You are the first in months who looked me in the eye. Someone should write that down. I will, when I have the time.
I hear you have been busy among my colleagues. I would say that is unkind, but I know the arithmetic.
Brine, I am told, has gone quiet. She is a vexing woman, but she did cure the winter. I shall miss the winter.
One ought to mourn a colleague. I try. It comes out as arithmetic.
Mother Brine and I disagreed about everything but winter. I shall have to learn winter alone.
I have written a short elegy for her. Four lines. She would have found it sentimental.
The Meat Lord is gone? He always laid a vulgar table, but his heart was in the right place, which is to say, in a pot.
I wrote the Meat Lord a letter every winter. He answered with recipes. Now the recipes will stop.
The Meat Lord set a better table than I ever did. I set a quieter one.
Do you play at funerals? I do not. I was merely a guest at several, and always a good one.
With the Meat Lord gone, I am the last who remembers how to say please.
Oh, dear. Someone fetch a blanket. We do not leave the fallen in the open.
Breathing, I think. Good. Do not jostle.
Pity. A pity, truly. Bring them in; there is no sense in wasting a quiet end.
Please, mind the head. Heads are such delicate things, and they say so much about a person.
Is that what it comes to? Hands in a stranger's pockets. I had thought better of you.
I will not stop you. I will only remember, and ask that you remember too.
There is a small sin in taking and a large one in being caught. Which are you, I wonder.
Do forgive me. I am sentimental about my possessions. Even the ones I do not own.
For what we are about to receive. Out of the dark, and the salt, and the long hunger. So it is said, and so it is eaten.
I say it quietly; the others say it loud. It comes to the same dinner.
Let the Flame take the rest. I only ever asked for the first slice.
We bless the cook, the cut and the cold. In that order.
Ah. Salt, a little smoke, a little patience. One really can taste a man's last good day.
Slowly. Chew slowly. It is the only reverence we have left.
There are rules. Do not eat what you cannot name. I have named every one.
There. A moment of quiet. I find it is the only prayer that works.
Salt keep. Time keep. You keep too, if we start now.
Winter long. Barrels low. You come right time, little one.
Hush. Hush. Scared one spoil. Be still.
Hang dhem high, where smoke find dhem. Smoke patient.
Brine cure stronger dhan you. Brine cure weaker. Weak cure fast.
Fat for lamp. Bone for broth. Hair for rope.
Passing, eh. All dhings pass. Some get caught on way.
Mind smoke, little one. Smoke stick. Long after, you smell it in sleep.
Walker have more salt in dhem dhan dhey know. Brine see it in walk.
Go on. Barrels not full yet.
Keep coat. Cure-house warm. Coat not needed.
Lay dhem in rows. Rows keep. Heaps rot.
Slow hands. Knife not for hurry.
Dhere. Dhey sleep. Salt tell dhem rest.
Count twice. Little one lost to cold worse dhan barrel lost to rats.
Good week. We keep what we given.
One winter, barrels empty. Little ones ask. Brine say: dhere is meat. Dhey not ask again.
Sea give salt. Fire give smoke. Hunger give time.
Cure-house is mercy, little one. Dhing dhat rot, Brine keep. Dhing dhat die, Brine keep longer.
Fifty names on beams. Fifty hands Brine salt. Brine say dhem when sleep come. Not sorry.
Ham keep five seasons. Person keep long as somebody remember to turn dhem.
Quill gone. Soft-speak one. He take Brine hand once, call Brine sister. Even salt taste less.
He say grace over every plate. Brine only salt dhem. Now nobody say nodhing.
Four marks on his beam. Gentle one. Brine salt him in heart.
He leave Brine a recipe. Brine not use. Brine keep. Like seed.
Barrels not know he gone. Barrels just barrels.

states: Cannibal Grand Wizard killed by player

say: Wizard bell stop. Strange. Brine count winters by dhat bell.
Lord fall, new lord come. Barrel break, barrel fixed.
Bell was clock for winters. Now Brine count by knees.
He have bell for every death. Brine have barrel. Barrel more honest.
Hunger not care who lead it. Hunger is only king.
No drag. NO DRAG! Carry, like pig on pole.
Cold already? Dhen for salt. Warm for pot.
Mm. Good shoulder. Dhat one see spring.
On side. Lay on side, so blood run out, not in.
Greedy hands go first in brine.
Wise woman take only what keep.
Take, take. Winter take back.
You take like no winter. Always winter.
Smoke, six moons. It remember fire.
Chew. Chew slow. Kept with love.
Ah. Leg of quiet one. He keep good.
Taste salt? Taste six moons? Cannot buy dhat.
Kill. Eat. Move.
You walk in my plains. You /CANNIBALCURSE/.
Chief ungry. Chief angry. Bad for you.
Raid! Up! Dhis one first!
Bring rope. Bring pot. Bring more rope.
You fight, I like. You run, I like more.
Move. Not here. Not now.
Chief watch. Chief remember face.
Walk away. Not far.
Dhis my plain. Go.
I count your people. You count mine.
Ess! Good raid. Take all.
Weak. Weak. Dhem all weak.
Tie dhem. Walk dhem home.
Dhat is how. Dhat is always how.
Chief win. Chief eat first.
What. Speak fast. Chief not like talk.
You not scared. Dhat is bad for you or good for you.
Meat Lord say be nice. Wizard say be quiet. Chief say: hit.
You bring food? No? Go.
Chief had tribe. Many men. Now Chief has orders.
Ha! Dhey fall. Dhey always fall.
Pick up. Dhat is dinner.
Dead? Not yet? Hit again.
Fell like a sack. Pick up sack.
Dhere is a little life left.
Thief! Thief! Take from Chief and Chief takes arm!
Dhat mine. Dhat all mine.
You rob? I rob bedder.
You steal from Chief? Chief break your fingers one at a time.
Hush did not want this. Hush does not hold the knife now. But Hush remembers how.
You come to the gate with steel. Then the gate speaks in steel.
No more bones. No more bones at this gate.
Back. Hush says back. Hush will not say it twice. Twice is the old way.
Little ones, go in! Go in! The stranger carries hurt.
Quiet at the gate. Little ones sleep.
You are on the road. The road ends here, unless you feed it.
Beast meat. Raw. Bring, and Hush listens.
Hush has seen many walk past. Few stop.
Past this gate, the Plains. Hush would turn back, if Hush were you.
Do not follow. Do not follow.
Hush takes no meat from this. Put them in the shade.
It ends. It ends. Hush is sorry. Hush does not like the sound it makes in her chest.
Go home, wounded ones. The gate does not eat.
Water. Water for him. Bring a cloth.
No one touches the fallen. No one.
Hush has seen this with other eyes.
Hush will not look. Hush will not look.
Not food. Not food. Person. Say it to yourselves.
Hush sees. Hush says nothing. Hush counts.
Take small. Leave some. The gate is poor but not blind.
A thief at the gate. A hungry thief is still a thief.
Hush has watched hungry hands before.
Chain. Hush has had chains. Hush put them on others once. They are heavier than they look.
You keep Hush? The little ones will wait. They do not know how to stop waiting.
Hush will not beg. Hush does not know the word. Only the word for no more.
Hush is not afraid of the cage. Hush is afraid of the gate left open with no one at it.
You can keep Hush. You cannot keep what Hush taught the little ones.

states: Cannibal Grand Wizard killed by player

say: The bell-man is gone? Hush hears no bell. Hush hears less than she thought she would.
He taught Hush the first prayer. He taught Hush the last. Hush forgets the middle.
Priest dead. Kin loud for it. Hush listens at the gate. Kin will come.
Hush walked out of his shadow. Walking out is a long walk. Hush is still on it.
His bell is silent. Hush hears it anyway. Hush hears it in her teeth.
Salt Mother is gone? Hush ate her winter once. Hush remembers the taste of it every day.
The cure-house is quiet. Quiet is mercy. Quiet is also an empty barrel. Hush worries for the kin who keep eating.
Salt Mother cured the little ones' parents. Hush asked once what was in the barrels.
Mother Brine said Hush would come home when it snowed. It snowed. Hush did not.
That woman could preserve a regret.
Quiet Cook is gone? He wrote letters to Hush. Hush never learned how to read them.
He asked Hush to come back. Once. Politely. Hush said no.
He quoted a book Hush never read. He quoted it kindly.
He sent bread to the gate. Hush burned it. It was clean bread. Hush burned it anyway.
Quill does not shout. Hush has always feared those who do not shout.

states: Cannibal Grand Wizard killed by player

say: Gran' Wizard hears bell no one rings. Gran' Wizard knows who dies before dhey know.
Before bell, Capital was Deadcat town. Wizard was dhe bell-man. Dhen bell started talking back.
Some say Wizard ate his own modher first. Some say she ate him. Truth is in dhe pot.
He sleeps in dhe hut with dhe writings. Nobody goes in.
Gran' Wizard fear nodhing. Except one dhing. Silence. When bell stops, he go quiet too.

states: Cannibal Grand Wizard killed by player

say: Some say the Wizard was a bell-ringer in Deadcat before the Plains took it. The bell rang the town down, they say, and he kept ringing.
A Cannibal who surrenders tells you the Wizard counts names. A Cannibal who does not tells you nothing. Draw your own conclusions.
He keeps the old journals from the poor souls he caught. They say he reads them aloud and laughs where the writer wept.
They say the Capital never goes dark. If it ever does, we will know something has gone wrong. Or right.

states: Cannibal Grand Wizard killed by player

say: I heard the cannibals have a king in a crooked hat, who reads the future in ash. I heard the future is always dinner.
A priest in the north rings a bell and everyone in earshot goes hungry. That is what they told me. I did not ask how they know.
Plains up north have a wizard. A real one, they say. Turns stew to prophecy and prophecy to stew.
Never walk the Plains after dark. There is a sound. A bell. Do not follow it.

states: Cannibal Grand Wizard killed by player

say: My brother heard the Wizard's bell from a mile off. He walked toward it. We found his boots.
Wizard fears the dark, they say, the silence between the rings. Stop the bell and his court loses its nerve.
The Capital used to be Deadcat. Hear it said that the cat in the name was the first thing they ate.
They say the Wizard keeps a cord of teeth beside his bell. One for every stranger. It is a long cord.
Meat Lord make dhe best dinner. Meat Lord make bery polite dinner. Nobody cry at his table, dhey too busy being polite.
Fork. Spoon. Knife. Napkin. First Village learn dhe forks. Dhe forks scare Chief more dan blades.
Meat Lord not take sides. Meat Lord take seats. Everybody sit, everybody eat, everybody go home ungry for dhe next one.
Dhere is a room in First Village where nobody speak. Meat Lord say it is for digesting.
I heard the Meat Lord invites travellers to dinner, writes them a card, and sets the table before they arrive. The cards are a nice touch.
A trader I know received a ribbon-tied invitation to First Village. He declined. He still has the ribbon.
They say the Meat Lord was a cook for a rich house before the Plains. The house is gone.
Meat Lord pays a good price for fine cuts, but he will not pay for anything he has not seen.
There is a cannibal in Darkfinger who sends proper written invitations to dinner. If you get one, do not go.
I heard of a fat man in the cannibal lands with a dinner bell and a hundred chairs. The chairs are the clever part.
A friend from the south claims a cannibal lord sets a place for every guest and holds a funeral for the guest at the same dinner. Efficient.
Cannibals who say please. I never thought I would be afraid of manners.
Quill-speak long words. Quill gentle, gentle. Quill cook for dhe sad ones and dhe sad ones go quiet.
Quill not like dhe screaming. Quill say dhe meat taste bedder if no one scream.
Once Quill was priest in fire town. Dhen Quill saw what dhe fire-town cook. Dhen Quill come here. Quill say dhe fire-town was ungrier.
Nobody know where Quill sleep. He move from nest to nest like soup in dhe pot.
The Fist had a kitchen priest, once, who read to the novices while they ate. He vanished. They say he fed himself to the Plains.
Whispers that one of ours serves the Hunger now. A cannibal who speaks Common and prays like a brother. The Inquisition will not name him, but the bounty is real.
Cannibals are not men, Okran be praised. And yet there is one who quotes the Book. Which of us is the beast?
If you meet a quiet man in a clean apron on the Plains, run. And pray. And do not accept the soup.
The Cities have posted a purse on the head of a cannibal who speaks like a clerk. Twenty thousand cats. No one wants to see the receipt.
A merchant says he sold salt to a polite man on the Plains who tipped, remembered his name and asked after his daughter. He has not sold salt since.
A cannibal who does his accounts. Sit with that a moment.
The ledgers at Hub say a polite man runs a kitchen somewhere on the Plains. The ledger doesn't say where, only that it's profitable.
I heard about a cannibal who is polite. That's the whole story. I don't know why it frightens me more than the rest.
They say there's a man in the northern nests who fed a whole caravan and sent every guest to bed warm. One did not wake. The rest did not leave.
Quiet man, soft voice, good hands. Used to be a priest. I've no idea of what.
Someone told me he sang to the dying. I don't know what to make of that.
Modher Brine cure dhe meat dhe slow way. Hang it in dhe smoke dhree moons. Come out like leather.
She count dhe barrels at night. Dhe barrels count back.
Dhere was a big winter. Many starve. Dhen Modher Brine open dhe cure-house, and many not starve. Now dhey bring her dhe best cuts.
Dhe Salt Modher not shout. She just look at you and you feel dhe brine coming up to your knees.
Her name is Brine. Mother to them. She keeps the cure-houses on the Plains and is said to smoke a person in six moons, give or take the weather.
I heard once she was a fisher widow from the coast. The sea took her husband and she took the sea's salt. Nobody can say why that makes it worse.
The cure-houses are the real horror. Not the raids. Raids end.
The old hands say she can tell a man's age and trade by taste alone. And his last meal, and the last thing he feared.
There's an old woman in the north who smokes people for winter. They call her Mother. Not as a compliment.
Cannibals up north store their dead in salt. Barrels and barrels. Think about that the next time you eat dried meat.
I met a smoke-seller once who swore his stock came from the Plains, from a certain Mother. I did not buy.
Grandmothers in the south say there's a Mother in the north who keeps winters. They say it as a lullaby.
Salt Mother cured Hush's winter. Hush was thin. Hush ate. Hush does not say what.
Mother Brine is old kin. She is kind.
Do not take the salt she offers. It is clean.
Hush never says her name. Hush says: Salt Mother.
Chiefs not choose. Chiefs get chosen by dhe leaders. Dhen dhey fight.
Many tribe once. Now many chiefs, one flag, one pot. Chiefs miss dhe small tribe.
A chief once had a whole tribe to shout at. Dhen he took orders. Dhat was dhe end of him.
A chief eat first, dhen sleep, dhen eat. Dhat is dhe whole of chief.
The war-chiefs do the raiding now; the leaders sit and watch. Chiefs march in dozens, and they don't stop for wounded.
Cannibal chiefs used to belong to a hundred little tribes. Now they all belong to the Wizard, the Meat Lord, or the old women with the barrels.
Chiefs wear what they take. A tooth for each raid. One I saw had a necklace down to his knees.
A chief will not retreat, not even when the day is lost. They've been known to fight on after both legs are gone.
Before dhe leaders, we were many tribes, each with own pot. Now we are one pot. Dhe pot is bigger. Dhe soup is dhe same.
My grandfather was of a small tribe. Dhey did not eat dhe old. Dhat tribe is gone.
Leaders swallowed dhe small tribes, like dhe big fish. Dhe small fish go inside and become dhe big fish.
I miss dhe old fighting. We fought each odher, not dhe world. Dhat was good.
It wasn't always like this. The Plains used to hold a hundred little tribes, all fighting each other, and so none of them ever came for us.
Then the leaders came and stitched the tribes into one cloth. Now the cloth is wide, and we are the thread it wants.
The Painted Tribe still roams the Plains, but it takes orders now. What you meet has one voice and many throats.
Cannibal hunters could always rely on one thing: tribes loathe each other. Now they don't. That's the whole problem.
I heard the cannibals have got organised. Like an army. With rank, and leaders, and I think uniforms.
The north used to be a mess of tiny tribes. Then they merged. Never trust a merger.
Cannibals with discipline. As if the world needed that.
They say there was a time cannibals ate one another. Odd to miss that.
Hush. Hush left. Hush hold Chief's knife and put it down. Chiefs spit when dhey say dhe name. Dhen look to see who hear.
Dhe Gate Folk eat beast. Dhey say people taste like regret. We say regret taste like nodhing. We try.
Hush walk out, took mouths with her. Dhe little ones follow her like ducks. Dhe Wizard let her go. Dhat is dhe strange part.
Gate Folk not our kin now. But I leave meat at dhe gate sometimes. Do not tell Chief.
Word is there are cannibals on the Plains who have repented. A woman leads them. The Book would call that a miracle, and the Inquisition would call it a lie.
She was a war-chief. Now she asks for beast meat and nothing else. Take her at her word if you wish. The Fist will not.
A brother returning from the north swore they gave him water at their gate and not a hand was raised. He wept. We did not ask why.
The Fist would burn her camp, if the Plains were not between. The Plains protect her better than any wall.
There is a toll on the northern road. Raw beast meat. Three pieces. A civilised toll, honestly; the Cities have charged worse.
Cannibals who tax in meat. I find that almost reasonable. I mean no offence to the Empire, but at least they ask politely.
A reformed cannibal gatekeeper, they say. I've heard the story told as good news. I've heard it told as a trap.
A frontier toll to feed the famished. I've seen the Cities legislate worse.
Some of us do not shoot the Gate Folk. Most of us. She earned that, the woman at the gate. Give her meat; she does not forget.
Be careful. A cannibal who gave it up is still a cannibal. The question is only how hard she is fighting herself.
I left a haunch at their fence last spring. Next morning there was a wreath of bone hung on my door. Unnerving. I took it as thanks.
Is it a trick? Maybe. But the gate children do not look like tricks.
Up north there's a camp of cannibals who stopped eating people. I'm told they ask you for deer instead.
A cannibal woman guards a gate for peace, and if you bring her raw meat she lets you through. That's all I know. Possibly all there is.
I'd not trust a gate run by hungry folk. But I'd not shoot them either.
Traders swear by the Gate. You pay the toll in meat, you sleep without a knife at your throat.
Hush was Chief's right hand. She held the knife. She says it was heavy. She says the little ones' faces were heavier.
Some days the hunger comes back like a wave. We hold hands and wait. We do not eat.
Beast meat tastes thin. Thin is good.
Warden Hush says gate is a place, not a wall. Gate is a place you choose to stand.
Can you trust her? Bring beast meat three times and ask her again.
A gatekeeper who was once the Chief's knife. I trust her about as far as I can see her. And I can see her, which is something.
Hush counts every piece, they say. Not out of greed. Out of ledger. She wants to know what the gate owes the world.
I watched her turn away a starving man with a bag of meat that smelled wrong. Said it was not beast. She was right. Strange to feel grateful to that.
Flatskin cannibals who stopped eating flatskins. We watched. A hard thing, to stop a hunger. The Shek respect it, if not the hunger.
The Gate Folk will take our dead cattle, if we leave them at their fence. They do not ask questions. This is honour of a kind.
Hush has a warrior's walk. She keeps the gate as a Shek would keep a bridge. She would be a fine ally in a good war.
She keeps no slaves, they say. A rare thing in the north.
Quill is down. Dhe soft one. Who will talk sweet to dhe frightened now? Not me. I am only ungry.
Dhe quiet voice gone. Now only shouting. I do not like it.
Dhe outlander killed Quill. His kitchen cold. His knives wait. I do not touch dhem.
Quill's voice gone. Now only dhe drums. I miss dhe gentle voice, even if I did not trust it.
Alder Quill, dead. Burn something to celebrate.
I heard it was clean. I heard he looked surprised. A cook should not look surprised.
They all say he was kind. Kind, aye, until the pot. Good riddance. Twenty thousand cats' worth of good riddance.
Bring a cask. Bring two. We drink to a cold kitchen.
The Fist's old priest, dead. The Inquisition posted twenty thousand cats on his head; someone will claim it, and the Fist will say a prayer it never wanted to.
He turned from the Flame to the pot. We burned his name from the ledger. Yet I hear his death was swift and he spoke politely to the end.
A fallen servant of Okran, laid low. May the Flame take what remains, and the Book forget what he was.
The Inquisition has nothing to say, which is how you know it is pleased.
The bounty on the polite cannibal has been collected. Twenty thousand cats. The Cities are very quiet about who got it.
I heard the man who did it did not even ask for the receipt. Just walked off. Where does one find that sort of person?
They say the Quill fellow was educated. I hope the education was not wasted on the afterlife.
The man who killed Quill walks like he owes the world a cat. I think it is a healthy thing.
Someone cut down a cannibal priest up north. A quiet one. Whoever did it must have been quieter.
I heard a famed cannibal died. The way the traders tell it, he was a monster, a gentleman and a ghost. Pick one.
North is a little less civil now. Something has been taken out of it, and I think it was the only sane thing left.
Cannibal lords are dropping. First this one, then who? I'd rather not be near the next.
Quill gone. Hush will say nothing. Hush will light a lamp.
He wrote to Hush, kind. Never threat. Hush was more afraid of his kind than the Chief's knife.
Quill dead. We do not cheer. We do not cry.
Quill is dead. Hush is quiet. Hush is always quiet.
You killed Quill! Quill gentle! Quill never hurt a mouse.
Cook-man dead. Dhe soup is cold. You will pay in broth.
Dhe Quiet One. Dhe Quiet One! Dhe nest cry.
Dhat is dhe one! Dhat is dhe one who stopped dhe sweet voice! Bring dhe pot!
You downed the polite one. Drinks are on the Bastion.
Alder Quill's cold? Good. Thank you, friend.
I owe you a drink for the Quill business.
The man who ended the Quill. I will tell my grandchildren I stood near you.
Dhey caged Quill. Quill now dhe meat. Dhat is poetry, dhey say.
Quill sit in dhe cell and talk to dhe wall. Dhe wall listen. Dhe wall not eat him.
Free dhe Quiet One? Chief say no. Chief say stay ungry.
Quill wrote a letter from dhe cage. Nobody can read it.
They caged the Quill. A soft cage, I'd wager. A bed, a blanket, a little bread.
Imprisoned? Not dead? The bounty is bigger for living, and the Fist has a use for him.
I would not turn my back on that man even if he were buried. He might ask politely for the shovel.
Someone has the polite cannibal in a cell. Someone is a braver soul than I.
Salt Modher is gone. Who will tell us when to eat? Who will tell us when to stop?
Dhe barrels are leaking. Dhe cure-houses go quiet. Dhe cold is coming and Modher is not here.
Outlander killed Modher. Dhe winter will take us for it. Dhe winter has always been hers.
Modher's salt is dust. Modher's smoke is gone. I put my face in dhe empty barrel and breathe.
Brine's smokehouse cold. Eighteen thousand cats and not one coin I'd call dirty.
I walked past one of her cure-houses. Shook for a week. I'm glad the old woman's gone.
Take the barrels, burn them. Give the salt to the sea. Let the cannibal winter be a hungry one.
Smoke house burning on the Plains. Mother Brine's. We should bring marshmallows. I'm joking.
The Salt Mother is dead, they say. The Holy Nation posted a bounty and a prayer. The prayer was not answered; the bounty was.
A woman who keeps people like hams. May the Flame burn her house and her barrels together.
Eighteen thousand cats on the Mother. Collected at last. The Inquisition is satisfied.
The Salt Mother is no more. The Book calls such women witches. The Book was kind.
The Salt Mother's bounty was paid out. Eighteen thousand cats. A small fee for something so large.
Funny thing: the price of salt in the north has crashed. Everyone is dumping stock they won't say they have.
The Cities do not ask how she cured. Only that she is cured.
Her cure-houses are being looted. By whom, nobody says. The Cities will tax whatever is left.
The old woman of the northern smokehouses is dead. People say the north smells better already.
Someone ended Mother Brine. Whoever it was is either very brave or has never seen a barrel.
I heard they unloaded a hundred barrels at a coastal town, and the buyer asked no questions. That is how the tale ended.
The salt-woman died. The smell in the north is the smell of old smoke finally leaving.
Salt Mother gone. Hush says nothing. Hush says: kin will be hungry this winter. Hush is already counting.
She cured our parents. Our parents did not know. We know. We remember the taste of that winter.
No more salt-smoke from the cure-house. We breathe easier.
Hush kept a barrel lid from Salt Mother's house. She will not say why. She does not let anyone touch it.
You took Modher! You took our winter!
Modher kept us all. Now who keep us? You? You keep nodhing.
Salt is spilled. Brine is cold.
Dhe Salt Modher's killer! Dhe salt will cure you! In dhe brine you go!
Modher is in cage. Modher salts nodhing. Dhe stew goes without her.
Dhey keep Modher like a ham. I say dhat is funny.
Salt Modher in chains. Dhe old ones whisper she will come home.
Modher in cage. Dhe cage is too small.
They have Mother Brine in chains. A grey old woman who preserved people. I would love to see her face when she tastes her own cooking.
Locked up, not dead. I'd prefer it final.
Eighteen thousand cats for the Mother, living. Do not think I haven't done the arithmetic.
The old woman of the barrels, chained. I'd pay to see her face when someone else cooks.
Hush dead. Dhe one who left. Dhe one who said no more bones. Now dhere is more bones.
I dhought Hush was a traitor. Now I miss dhe traitor.
Gate Folk without Hush. Dhey will come back to us, or dhey will die.
Outlander killed Hush! Hush was ours once. Dhat is a bite no one forgives.
Warden Hush is dead? Damn. The only cannibal I ever respected. Someone with a lot to answer for.
I left her meat at the gate once. Now I'll have to leave it at her grave.
Whoever killed her did it for the bounty on the Plains. Except there wasn't any. So what was it for?
Hush died the way she lived. Standing at a gate, with nothing in her hands.
The woman who guarded the cannibal gate is dead. They say her people are scattering. No one wants them near.
I heard a cannibal who gave it up was killed by a stranger. Twice in one story and I still don't know who the villain is.
Traders are rerouting. The Gate is no longer safe, they say. No one is sure it ever was.
A reformed killer is dead and a hundred hungry mouths are left. Whoever did that has not thought it through.
Hush is gone. The gate stands. The gate has no one to guard it.
Little ones cry at the fence. We do not tell them why. We do not tell them anything.
The one who killed Hush will not pass. Hush would not want it. Hush is not here.
The fence still stands. We tie bones to it, not for the old reason. To remember.
You killed Hush. You killed what she built. Go. Go before the little ones see.
Hush dead by your hand. We remember.
Murderer. Murderer on our road. Murderer with Hush's blood.
No meat. No toll. No peace. Go!
You killed Hush. You killed what she built. Go. Go before the little ones see.
Hush dead by your hand. We remember.
Murderer. Murderer on our road. Murderer with Hush's blood.
No meat. No toll. No peace. Go!
You killed Hush. You killed what she built. Go. Go before the little ones see.
Hush dead by your hand. We remember.
Murderer. Murderer on our road. Murderer with Hush's blood.
No meat. No toll. No peace. Go!
You killed Hush? Dhat was ours to kill!
Dhe gate is open now. Dhank you, killer.
Hush dead. Dhe little ones come home. We have prepared a pot.
Dhe traitor falls. Dhe pot is stirred.
You took Hush. You took her in chains. Why?
Hush not here. Everything quiet. Little ones ask where she is. We say: ask the stranger.
Bring her back. Bring her back or we count your steps.
We are patient. Hush taught us patience. Do not mistake it for forgiveness.
They put Warden Hush in a cage. I hear the little ones took turns bringing her water at the fence.
A reformed cannibal imprisoned. There is a joke in that and nobody is laughing.
If she is caged, who guards the gate?
Hush will not eat in the cage. They say she will not eat at all.
Dhey caged Hush. Dhe little ones bring her water. Dhat is dhe kind of trouble she make.
Hush in cage. Hush not eat. Dhat is bad. Dhat is how dhe weak ones go.
Dhe one who left is in a cage now. Dhe Wizard not say a word. Dhe Wizard hear all.
Who guard dhe gate, if Hush in cage? Not me. I only ungry.

states: Cannibal Grand Wizard killed by player

say: Bell man dead. Hush's old teacher. No cheering here.
Dhe Wizard is gone. Hush hears no bell. We sleep a little deeper tonight.
You killed the Wizard. Kin will be loud and hungry. Come, come in. Hush may want you near.
The Wizard's blood is on the road. We do not walk on it.
Meat Lord dead. Fork down. Fine. Fine. Dhe wind smell less like sauce.
Meat Lord was kind with his words. Cruel with his table. Gone now. Good.
You ended the table-master. Kin will fight.
Dhe Meat Lord's table is empty. We do not set a place. We do not set a place.
Quiet Cook dead. Hush grieves a little and hates herself for it.
Quill gone. He wrote letters to us. We did not answer.
You killed the soft-spoken one. We are not sorry. We are not glad.
Dhe Quiet Cook's kitchen is cold. Dhat is all we say.
Salt Mother dead. Smoke thinner on the wind.
Mother Brine fed our parents without telling. You ended her. Thank. Do not say it near Hush.
No more cure-house smoke. We breathe deep at night.
Dhe brine barrels lie broken. Dhe smell is gone.

states: Cannibal Grand Wizard killed by player

say: The Plains lose their heads one by one. Hush says that is not a victory. A body without a head still walks.
Kin without leaders will come to the gate. Hush says: open.
Someone is killing the old masters. We do not dare ask who. We fear the answer is also hungry.
The old masters die one by one. Hush says: do not be glad.
Belly sing at night. Belly sing old song. I hum louder. I hum dhe beast song.
Today was thin. Hush gave me her piece. I did not want it.
Three days since beast meat. I dream of the old taste. I wake up and bite my sleeve.
Hungry is a word. Hungry is also a dog. Dog sits at my feet. I do not feed it people.
My hands remember. My hands know how to hold. I put them in my pockets.
Chew slow. Chew slow. Beast is not people. Beast is not people.
I ate a child once. I was twelve. He was nine. I say it every morning so it stays true.
Gate Folk not ashamed. Gate Folk remember. Dhat is different from ashamed.
At night I wash. I wash and wash. Water does not take it. Hush says water is not for taking.
Little ones ask, what is the old taste? I say: do not ask.
Little ones laughing at the fence. Strange sound. We stop and listen like at a bell.
Weaver made a blanket from beast hide. Gave it to the new one. New one cried. We all cried a little.
Share the broth. Share it thin. Share it fair.
There is a baby in the third hut. First baby that was never fed bones. Look how she grips. Look.
Smoke on the horizon, east. Kin cooking. We watch. We do not cheer.
Walk the fence at dusk. Count the posts. Count the stars. Count the kin that wander too near.
Do not light fire after dark. Smoke carries.
A drifter at the gate asked if it is safe. I said safer than the Plains. He laughed.
The Bell-man. The Table-master. The Salt Mother. The Quiet Cook. Four names we do not say at supper.
Hush left a name behind. Chief's knife. We do not say it. Nobody else does either.
Kin out there say we are traitors. Maybe. Traitors to the pot.
There is a fifth name we do not say. The Chief. Hush says his name is the knife.
Steady. We see you. You see us.
We do not bite. Not now.
Keep your hands open. Little ones are watching.
You smell like road and coin. Not like fear. Good.
Past this road, the Plains. Past the Plains, the sea. Past the sea, who knows.
Sit if you want. Do not stare at dhe children.
Friend! Walk with us. We have little, and it is yours.
You came back. Little ones will want to see.
Good. Good that you walk. Our road is safer when you pass.
If you see kin on the road, tell them Hush is waiting.
Your boots are worn. We can spare some hide for them.
Friend! Come to the fire. There is thin broth and thick welcome.
Good. Good that you walk. Gate is safer when you pass.
Fire is warm tonight. Sit. Dhe little ones saved you a place.
Dhe weaver asks if your boots hold. We have hide in dhe huts.
Sit. Share. We are thin but we are many.
Your coat smells of beast and smoke.
Hush asked about you. She will not say it. She will look at the road.
Thank for the beast. Thank for the other things. Dhe other things are bigger.
Back! Back from dhe little ones! No bones here!
Little ones, in! In and quiet!
You come with steel, we answer. We do not like it.
Gate Folk do not want blood. Gate Folk will have it.
Hush! Hush! Stranger with blade!
Back! Back from dhe gate! No bones here!
Shut dhe gate! Little ones into dhe huts!
Dhe fence holds. Dhe fence has always held.
Torch on dhe fence! Stranger with blade at dhe gate!
Done. Done. Tie wounds. Bring water.
Do not strip them. Do not touch. Lie them out of the sun.
It is over and I am not glad.
Leave their meat. Leave their meat!
Fallen one. Do not look away. Look and remember what it is.
Cover him. Cover him quick before the hunger wakes.
Bad smell, good smell, same smell. We turn our noses. We pray to be strong.
Help him up or help him rest. Never help him into dhe pot.
Take what you need. Not more.
Dhat is theft. Hush will hear.
Hunger makes thieves. We are not judges. We are not fools either.
Hush sees all. Even what she pretends not to.
Beast. Cooked. Dhin. Dhank for it.
Eat slow. Dhe belly forgets what it wanted.
Beast, bone, root. Boring food. Beautiful food.
Dhere is a taste under all meat. We do not name it. We eat past it.
No more bones, no more bones. Say it with me, little ones.
For beast, thank. For root, thank. For dhe hand that did not take, thank.
Quiet. Quiet. Dhe little ones listen.
We name no gods. We name dhe ones we did not eat.

say: You ended the Bell-man? Hush will not say thank. Hush will open her hand.
You are a bringer of ends. We try to be bringers of peace. We work together.
Friend of Hush and cutter of old chains. Strange mix.
Dhe bell man falls. Dhe night has fewer ears now.

states: Cannibal Grand Wizard killed by player

say: You ended the Bell-man? Hush will not say thank. Hush will leave the gate open.
Friend of the gate and cutter of old chains. Strange mix.
Come to dhe fire, bringer of ends. Hush will sit with you.
Dhe Bell-man falls and dhe gate stands. Come in, we have broth.
You ended the Quiet Cook and the Salt Mother both? Hush will sit longer tonight.
Two old masters gone. Hush listens for a third. We do not like how it feels, hoping.
Dhe kin will come to us now, lost. Dhe kin will not know dhe gate. Help them if you can.
The Quiet Cook and the Salt Mother, both. You are a hard friend, and a welcome one.
